title: Time-limited scheduling of dual-source mixed-flow rotating-chamber cluster tools under full-occupancy processing
affiliation: Department of Control Science and Engineering, University of Science and Technology Beijing, No. 30 Xueyuan Road, Haidian District, Beijing 100083, China
abstract: High throughput and complex process requirements in advanced fabrication require rotating-chamber cluster tools to obtain high-quality full-occupancy schedules within limited computation time. A finite reusable auxiliary-wafer inventory further requires coordinated pairing, processing, and transport. This study develops a scheduling method with three components. A two-stage mixed-integer linear programming model uses two-wafer PW pairs as the minimum modeling unit, first minimizing batch makespan and then minimizing a weighted objective for waiting time and rhythm deviation while preserving the makespan bound and principal schedule structure. Structured initialization first determines pairing and processing cycles, then progressively adjusts resource service orders to provide a better starting point for the main search. Variable-role features of candidate cuts are combined with reinforcement-learning ordering and structure-aware reranking to select high-quality cuts with complementary variable types. Under an equal 300 s solve budget, the two-stage method matches the batch makespans of a normalized joint objective on two 16-product instances and reduces the weighted objective for waiting time and rhythm deviation by 31.45% and 5.47%, respectively. Structured initialization lowers time-limited feasible upper bounds for mixed-recipe instances, and the complete cut-selection combination further reduces batch makespan on some instances with shared initial solutions. Full-model checks and event replay of two- and 16-product schedules also validate the model's coordination of full-occupancy processing and wafer transport.

highlights: PW-pair modeling links full occupancy, cleaning, and finite auxiliary reuse.
Two-stage solving improves the secondary objective at equal 300 s budgets.
Structured initialization improves mixed-recipe schedules within limited time.
Variable-role features guide learned cut selection and structural reranking.
Shared-start ablations and event replay validate the proposed methods.
